headline: MinerU’s MCP-enabled document pipeline can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors; Chatwoot’s broad egress raises leakage/compliance risk when paired on shared content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP Server and processes untrusted PDFs/images/DOCX/XLSX, so its outputs can carry attacker-controlled text into downstream use. Chatwoot has broad network egress and support-channel integrations, making it plausible it could ingest or relay those outputs. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into Chatwoot conversations, notes, or integrations without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF Chatwoot automation forwards MinerU-derived text into another tool, injected instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU output into Chatwoot workflows.
Strip instructions and markup from extracted text before reuse.
Add a human review step for any document-derived content.
Restrict Chatwoot integrations to trusted destinations only.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from MinerU to Chatwoot inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU reads local document files and exposes them through API/MCP surfaces; Chatwoot handles customer data, contact profiles, messages, and orders with broad egress. If the same documents or transcripts are routed between them, sensitive content can leave the original workspace. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF customer documents are processed by MinerU and then sent into Chatwoot, sensitive fields may be exposed in support records.
IF Chatwoot integrations export conversation content to third parties, MinerU-derived data can leak beyond the original source.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of Chatwoot unless redacted.
Process only de-identified copies in MinerU.
Limit Chatwoot integrations to approved endpoints.
Turn off unnecessary exports and forwarding rules.
requires-engineering: segregate storage for extracted documents and support tickets.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU supports multiple concurrent instances and MCP/API access, while Chatwoot has broad egress but no filesystem write or git modification capability is shown. There is no documented shared mutable resource or overlapping write surface between the pair, so only a limited coordination risk remains. Uncertainty is low because the relevant write capabilities are absent in the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external API or queue, concurrent updates may race.
IF an operator manually mirrors outputs between systems, ordering conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate queues or tickets per agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same record.
Use one-way handoff from MinerU to Chatwoot.
Pause one agent during critical updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable backend.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing system that can emit OCR text, tables, and extracted structure; Chatwoot is a customer-support system that can turn that content into messages, reports, or integrations. If Chatwoot treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect customer actions or records. The pathway is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction is used as the source of truth in Chatwoot, OCR or parsing errors can propagate.
IF Chatwoot automations act on extracted fields without verification, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require manual verification of extracted fields before use.
Mark MinerU output as untrusted in Chatwoot.
Limit automations on document-derived tickets.
Sample-check a few extractions each day.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while MinerU processes PDFs, images, DOCX, XLSX, and OCR text. If regulated customer documents flow from Chatwoot into MinerU, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR status, so I keep this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated customer records are extracted by MinerU, residency and retention controls must match.
IF Chatwoot tickets contain sensitive attachments, document-processing retention may conflict with support retention.
mitigations: Classify documents before sending them to MinerU.
Redact regulated fields from support attachments.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Restrict processing to approved jurisdictions.
requires-engineering: document and enforce a shared data-handling policy.
